title: Bloodwork
full_review:
A medically compromised FBI agent is drawn back into the risky business of catching a cunning serial killer in the unexceptional thriller, "Blood Work" (Warner Bros.).

The movie is based on the same-titled 1998 novel by Michael Connelly with a screenplay by Oscar winner (for "L.A. Confidential") Brian Helgeland.

Surprisingly, the film sometimes looks as tired as the character Clint Eastwood plays, crack FBI profiler Terry McCaleb, who was forced into medical retirement after suffering a massive heart attack while pursuing the same serial killer who is about to bedevil his life once more.

Reclusive Terry has moved onto a houseboat and recently received a heart transplant, but a new victim's sister, Graciella(Wanda De Jesus), tracks him down with an offer he can't refuse. He should find her sister's killer out of respect, since it is now her heart that is beating in his chest and calling out for justice.

Hiring an eager houseboat neighbor, Buddy (Jeff Daniels), as his chauffeur, Terry begins to find a disturbing pattern to the latest homicides: their common link relates to him, personally. The killer has specifically targeted them to lure Terry back into the chase.

Meanwhile, Terry's cardiologist (Angelica Huston) insists he not resume the stressful hunt or she'll drop him as her patient. But, as he begins to bond with Graciella and the victim's young son (Mason Lucero), he's more compelled than ever to nail the relentless killer.

Also produced and directed by Eastwood, the film proceeds methodically if not energetically to its ultimate showdown. The dark visuals throughout are sleekly efficient but it has the too-familiar quality of an Eastwood cop character tracking down his prey until that final moment when one or the other is sure to die. The narrative relies on a sordid plot twist but loses credibility when the killer can predict exactly when Terry will identify him, plunging the two into a potboiler-type climax. In the violent finale one character is justified in responding with force -- but another late arriver to the scene is not.

All in all, not enough of "Blood Work" works to qualify as a suspenseful thriller.

Due to intermittent violence and rough language, a sexual situation and occasional profanity, the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops classification is A-III -- adults. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted.
